attacks.unsupported_mechanism: KILLED - claimed 4-log kill in 0.2 s using 12 kW pulsed UV-C LED; UV-C LED wall-plug efficiencies and optical intensities in seawater cannot deliver the order-of-magnitude tens to hundreds of J/cm² dose required for 4-log inactivation of organisms (UV doses of 40–100+ mJ/cm² are standard, meaning 0.2 s requires hundreds of kW of optical output, not 12 kW electrical), so the causal chain of dose-to-kill cannot hold.
attacks.weak_transfer: KILLED - the candidate transfers "UV-C inactivation" from bench collimated-beam / thin-film reactors (where Beer-Lambert fluence is well-defined) to a sea-chest grating ring where entrained flow is unlaminar, particles/organisms are shadowed by the grating bars, and 80 NTU turbidity is specified — UV transmittance in ballast water at 80 NTU is typically <30%/cm, so the bench-derived 4-log fluence does not transfer to the sea-chest geometry under the stated turbidity boundary.
attacks.prior_art: SURVIVE (firewall: prior_art_state=UNRESOLVED_INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is a non-kill state; adversarial PRIOR_ART=KILL is forbidden)
attacks.engineering_infeasibility: KILLED - 12 kW pulsed LED ring at a sea-chest grating is infeasible: UV-C LED arrays at this power require substantial driver/cooling mass and volume, and pulsed operation at kW-class with the required ~270 nm peak and sub-microsecond rise is beyond commercial UV-C LED capability (current pulsed UV-C LEDs deliver watts, not kilowatts, per array).
